root_idea.summary: The root has three principal lexical axes: a funnel or receptacle that admits liquid, coercive subjugation or forcible restraint, and a term for a large blue fly. The Quranic form belongs to the coercive instrument branch.
root_idea.development: The lexical evidence relates funneling and subjugation through the idea of something being forced inward or brought under control, while several specialized nouns arise through resemblance or conventional naming.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the singular dictionary citation form مِقْمَع, whose Quranic broken plural مَقَامِعُ is the supplied occurrence.

senses.definition: A mace, club, or other implement used to strike and subdue.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence is the broken plural مَقَامِعُ in the expression مَقَامِعُ مِنْ حَدِيدٍ, referring to iron instruments of punishment and subjugation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A funnel or receptacle through which liquid is poured.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Variant vocalizations قَمْع and قَمَع are also reported. In the expression أَقْمَاعُ القول, ears are figuratively likened to funnels when people hear speech without retaining or understanding it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To consume all of the liquid contained in a vessel or waterskin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized verb based on the image of liquid entering a funnel; the cited construction is اقتَمَعْتُ ما في السقاء.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To humble, overpower, or forcibly restrain; also, to strike someone with a mace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb may describe subjugation directly or an action performed with a مِقْمَع.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To drive a person back or repel him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with a person as the object of the act of rejection or forced withdrawal.
A specialized animal name; the lexical explanation connects the name with being driven or beaten away.
Used especially of a donkey driving away the blue flies that settle on it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The uppermost part of a camel’s hump, above the spinal projections.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical term for the top of the camel’s hump.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thickening in one of a horse’s knees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized term for an abnormal or pronounced thickening of the knee.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fleshy bump or excrescence at the eye-corner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical term for excess flesh forming in the موق, the corner of the eye.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The basal part of a date, the material adhering around its stalk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized term used of the date fruit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The meatus or canal of the ear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical expression referring to the ear passage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The choice portion or best selection of a people’s wealth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic expression for the finest part of a group’s property or possessions.

Defines the specialized basal part of a date and points onward for comparison.
Pointer-only reference to a plural form elsewhere.
Defines a specialized anatomical term for the ear meatus.

cautions: The supplied Quran occurrence is the plural مَقَامِعُ; the public headword is normalized to the singular citation form مِقْمَع on the basis of the explicit lexical evidence.
The contextual rendering “hooked rods” illustrates the supplied occurrence, while the lexical definition is the independently supported function of striking and subduing.
